findings.text: _is_node_contract_refusal restates the node-contract half of _is_until_changed_failure, which the same module already owns at holds.py:993-1000 (_NODE_CONTRACT_REFUSAL in text and _CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REMEDY not in text), and obligations.py:1807-1813 keeps a third inline copy of the same two clauses. The three agree today, so no behaviour differs, but a change to what counts as a node-contract refusal now has three places to miss; the owner should be one predicate that the other two call (the reverse works too: _is_until_changed_failure could be 'CompetenceLimit: in text or _is_node_contract_refusal(text)').

the row's next_command renders literal placeholders ('--done-when <measure>', '--brief <file>', '--write-path <path>', '--time-budget <budget>') straight into a string a session may copy, so running it as printed passes '<measure>' as the value; a rendered form should quote the placeholder or name the field without a shell-ready angle-bracket token, since the row's whole point is that its remedy changes the field the refusal names.

the agreed-pass counter increments whenever the previous stamped failure is a node-contract refusal, without comparing the contract fingerprint it was refused about; a request parked and then requeued with an unrelated contract refusal carried over from before would reach the two-pass threshold on its first reading after the repair. The stamp check in _retry_backoff_hold still releases it on a healthy read, so the effect is confined to a re-refused-repaired contract, but counting only an agreed *contract* would make 'two passes that each read the request' literal.
